name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Implement A/B testing for the new feature with 5% of users. This lets us measure real impact before scaling, reducing risk of a bad rollout. The trade-off is slower feedback—we won’t see results as quickly as a 10% blind rollout, but we avoid exposing more users to unproven changes. Data from 5% gives us enough signal to decide without gambling on a larger group.

name: Gauge
text: A 5% A/B test still risks missing critical edge cases—self-selection bias skews results if only engaged users opt in, and a 10% blind rollout to opted-in users repeats the same flaw. Instead, run a 10% blind rollout to *all* users, then split the data post-hoc to simulate A/B for validation. Settle it by comparing error rates and user drop-off between the two groups after one week.
